content:
The White House drew fierce backlash Thursday over an 18-second video promoting Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

“Peace through strength,” the White House captioned the clip, which went viral with more than 4.8 million views on X alone by early Friday.

The Atlantic’s David Frum, a former speechwriter for President George W. Bush, mocked: “Xi stole Trump’s lunch, ate it in front of him, and then made Trump dab Xi’s mouth with Trump’s napkin.”

Bestselling author Don Winslow said Trump and his administration “are just idiots who don’t understand foreign policy.”

“This is the wrong video at the wrong time and conveys the wrong message,” he added. “’Peace through strength’ was a direct quote from Nixon. It failed then. It’s failing now.”

Former Rep. Denver Riggleman (R-Va.) asked: “When did we become a cuckacracy? Turn against what we are… turn to darkness. Every American servicemember needs to see this ― see what their Commander in Chief really is.”

Former Rep. Adam Kinzinger (R-Ill.) questioned: “In what way did you show strength?” He then pointed to Trump’s friendly greeting of Putin as “my friend.”

Russian chess grandmaster and outspoken Putin critic Garry Kasparov called the video an “eternal humiliation.”

And former U.S. Ambassador to Israel Dan Shapiro described it as “the most pathetic thing I’ve ever seen.”

“That the White House think this projects strength is ridiculous,” he added. “It shows nothing but weakness: Trump desperate for the approval of our biggest competitors and adversaries, yet gaining nothing. What a joke.”
